curation.lead:
Roberta Schuhalter Karp (born 1958, Livingston, New York), known as Robbie Karp, is a corporate attorney and social impact consultant who spent more than two decades as Senior Vice President of Corporate Affairs and General Counsel at Liz Claiborne Inc. (SEC CIK 0000352363), later serving as SVP Business Development and Legal Affairs at Kate Spade & Company. Educated at SUNY Binghamton (BS Environmental Studies) and Hofstra University School of Law (JD 1983, Articles Editor of Law Review), she was admitted to the New York Bar in 1984 and began her career at Kramer Levin Naftalis & Frankel before joining Liz Claiborne in 1986, where she rose from Legal Counsel to the company's top legal officer. SEC insider filings confirm she held 38,703 shares of LIZ common stock as of her Form 3 filing in May 2007 (SEC CIK 1401123). She is the wife of Brad Karp, who served as chairman of Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP until his resignation on February 4, 2026, following the disclosure of his extensive email correspondence with Jeffrey Epstein.

Karp's investigative significance lies at the intersection of three domains. First, her role as Liz Claiborne's General Counsel during the CNMI/Saipan garment worker crisis of the late 1990s, when both Liz Claiborne and Les Wexner's The Limited were named as co-defendants in RICO and peonage class actions representing 30,000 trafficked workers. Three parallel lawsuits were filed in 1999, settling for $20 million in 2004 with no admission of wrongdoing. Simultaneously, Karp co-chaired President Clinton's White House Apparel Industry Partnership (1996–1999), which created a voluntary self-regulation framework — the Fair Labor Association — that critics described as a toothless substitute for federal legislation that Jack Abramoff was simultaneously lobbying to block. Second, her family's social relationship with Epstein: while Robbie Karp's name appears zero times across the entire 690,000-document Epstein corpus (DOJ Vol 11, DugganUSA, LMSBAND, Unified), both Karp children — David and Meredith — attended an Epstein-organized Woody Allen screening in May 2014 alongside Eva Dubin, Glenn Dubin, and Jes Staley (EFTA02383641). Epstein referenced Robbie obliquely in emails to Brad, noting her views on Charlie Rose's firing in November 2017 (EFTA02564029) and joking about her shared April 19 birthday with Kathryn Ruemmler (EFTA02466803).

Third, Karp occupies a distinctive position in the philanthropic and social impact sector that overlaps with network figures. She served as President of the Perelman Family Foundation (2014–2015) — Ronald Perelman appears on page 43 of the Epstein black book and Paul Weiss also represents Perelman's MacAndrews & Forbes. In 2015, she co-founded Karp Randel LLC, a social impact consultancy advising clients including Uber and the NFL on sexual assault and domestic violence programs, while simultaneously serving as Chairman of The Educational Alliance Inc., Secretary and Director of Human Rights First, and Director of The Chazen Fund to Address Domestic Violence. Despite this substantial professional profile, she maintains a remarkably minimal financial footprint: zero entries across eight corporate registries, zero UCC filings, zero lobbying records, zero court appearances as a party, zero ICIJ offshore records, and zero appearances in Deutsche Bank's DS10 transaction records. Her documented financial activity is limited to modest FEC donations ($250–$1,000 to Democratic candidates from 2004 to 2023, totaling approximately $10,500), SEC insider filings for Liz Claiborne (2007–2008), and an ACRIS executor role for the Estate of Sondra Karp alongside Brad Karp in 2010.

sections.title: Liz Claiborne, Saipan, and the Apparel Industry Partnership
sections.content:
Robbie Karp joined Liz Claiborne Inc. in 1986 as Legal Counsel and rose over two decades to Senior Vice President of Corporate Affairs and General Counsel, a trajectory confirmed by SEC filings spanning FY2001 through FY2008 (SEC CIK 0000352363). SEC 10-K filings for fiscal years 2000 through 2003 explicitly listed Saipan in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands as a sourcing country for Liz Claiborne garments, alongside approximately 38 other nations. From 1996 to 1999, concurrently with her senior role at Liz Claiborne, Karp co-chaired President Clinton's White House Apparel Industry Partnership, described as "the business side's point person on sweatshops." The AIP produced a Code of Conduct and created the Fair Labor Association as a voluntary, industry-led monitoring body.

The AIP framework was controversial from inception. Two labor unions and the Interfaith Center on Corporate Responsibility walked out, characterizing the voluntary self-regulation approach as inadequate. The timing is structurally significant: during the same period that Karp was co-chairing an industry effort to create voluntary standards, Jack Abramoff was receiving millions from the CNMI government to kill federal legislative reform. Abramoff successfully blocked 29 bills that would have extended actual federal labor law to Saipan. The voluntary framework that emerged from Karp's AIP was precisely the alternative that the garment industry and its lobbyists needed — a credible-sounding substitute for enforceable law, produced by the very companies that benefited from the regulatory gap.

In 1999, three class actions were filed on behalf of 30,000 garment workers in Saipan who had been subjected to conditions that the Department of the Interior documented as including forced labor, forced abortions, and sex trafficking. The lawsuits — proceeding under RICO, the Alien Tort Claims Act, and FLSA — named 26 retailers as defendants. Both Liz Claiborne (where Karp served as General Counsel) and The Limited (Les Wexner's company) were among the defendants. Liz Claiborne was not initially named but was "advised in writing" it would be added as a party if no consensual resolution was reached, and it entered settlement negotiations. The cases settled for $20 million in 2004 with no admission of wrongdoing. The convergence is notable: Alexander Acosta, who later gave Jeffrey Epstein the 2008 sweetheart plea deal, resigned as Secretary of Labor in July 2019 and was replaced by Patrick Pizzella — who had lobbied alongside Abramoff to block the very worker protections that would have applied to factories supplying Karp's and Wexner's companies.

sections.title: The Epstein Relationship and Systematic Name Avoidance
sections.content:
Robbie Karp's name does not appear a single time across the entire Epstein document corpus — a verified negative result spanning 331,000 DOJ Vol 11 pages, 204,000 DugganUSA documents, 60,000 LMSBAND files, 70,000 Unified DB records, and 25,000 Epstein 20K documents. The 91 DugganUSA hits returned for "Robbie Karp" are all references to Roberta Kaplan, Esq. of Kaplan Hecker & Fink LLP, who represented Epstein victims in USVI compensation proceedings and is an entirely different person. Searches for "Schuhalter" and "Sondra Karp" likewise returned zero results. This absence is notable because both Karp children, David and Meredith, do appear by name in the corpus.

On May 19, 2014, Epstein organized a private Woody Allen film screening attended by Eva Dubin, Glenn Dubin, Brad Karp, David Karp, Meredith Karp, Jes Staley, Staley's wife, and Staley's daughter Alexa (EFTA02383641). Robbie Karp was conspicuously not listed as an attendee at this family event where both her children were present. In July 2015, Brad told Epstein "I think I'm coming solo tonight. My son just had some minor knee surgery yesterday" (EFTA02494288), the phrasing implying that Robbie's attendance at Epstein social events was sometimes expected. A July 21, 2015 scheduling note from Epstein assistant Bebe Avdiu listed a dinner with Woody Allen and Soon-Yi with "Brad Karp and his so[n]" — again referencing Brad and a child but not Robbie (EFTA02340072).

Epstein demonstrated personal familiarity with Robbie on at least two documented occasions. On November 21, 2017, the day Charlie Rose was fired from CBS and PBS for sexual misconduct, Epstein emailed Brad with the subject line "charlie" and the message "I guess your wife can feel vindicated :)" — to which Brad replied "Jeez. She certainly does not feel special" (EFTA02564029). The exchange implies that Robbie had previously expressed negative views about Rose to Epstein personally, and that Epstein remembered and referenced them months or years later. On April 19, 2018, Epstein texted Brad that it was Kathryn Ruemmler's birthday. Brad responded: "My wife's too. I'll never forget Kathy's birthday!" Epstein replied: "you can tell your wife, it is kathys that you always remember — so your wife is safe" (EFTA02466803). The shared April 19 birthday created an annual reminder linking the Karp household to the Epstein-Ruemmler connection. Throughout all these exchanges, Epstein consistently referred to Robbie as "your wife," never using her name — a pattern that, combined with the total absence of "Robbie Karp" from the document corpus, suggests deliberate avoidance.

sections.title: Philanthropic Networks and the Perelman Foundation
sections.content:
After leaving the corporate sector, Karp constructed a second career in nonprofit governance and social impact consulting. She served as President of the Perelman Family Foundation from 2014 to 2015, a role that placed her at the center of a triple nexus connecting the Karp family, the Perelman orbit, and the broader Epstein-adjacent social world. Ronald Perelman appears in Epstein's black book on page 43 with two phone numbers and one address. Perelman hosted a 1995 Clinton fundraiser in Palm Beach that Epstein attended. And Paul Weiss, where Brad Karp served as chairman, has long represented Perelman's MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings. The philanthropic, legal, and social connections between the Karp family and the Perelman-Epstein sphere thus converge through multiple independent channels.

In 2015, Karp co-founded Karp Randel LLC with Jane Randel, a social impact consultancy whose clients have included Uber and the NFL for work on sexual assault and domestic violence programs. The entity has no corporate registration in New York Secretary of State records, no entries in the SEC EDGAR database, and no filings in any of the eight corporate registries searched — it appears in a single FEC donation record from January 2022 listing Karp as co-president. Her board positions encompass Chairman of The Educational Alliance Inc., Secretary and Director of Human Rights First, Director of The Chazen Fund to Address Domestic Violence (created by Jerome Chazen, who chaired Liz Claiborne during her tenure), and board member of the Charles H. Revson Foundation. She was a David Rockefeller Fellow at the Partnership for New York City from 2000 to 2001. The thematic consistency of her post-corporate work — human rights, domestic violence, labor standards — stands in tension with her professional history as General Counsel of a company that sourced from jurisdictions where documented forced labor and sex trafficking of garment workers occurred.

sections.title: Financial Profile and Documentary Absence
sections.content:
For a former Fortune 500 Senior Vice President and the wife of one of New York's most prominent law firm chairmen, Robbie Karp maintains a remarkably thin financial footprint. Her FEC donation records from 2004 through 2023 show 21 contributions totaling approximately $10,500 to Democratic candidates, including Jerry Nadler ($1,000 in 2022 and 2023), Cheri Beasley ($1,000), Kathy Manning ($1,000), Scott Cooper ($1,000), John Fetterman ($250), Kirsten Gillibrand ($250), and a 2004 contribution to Jamie Metzl listing her employer as "Liz Claiborne Senior VP." Post-2020 donations list her employer as Karp Randel LLC. These are modest amounts — $250 to $1,000 per candidate — compared to Brad Karp's visible political giving, which exceeds $100,000 in recent cycles and includes $25,000 to the Harris Victory Fund and $15,000 to the DSCC in September-October 2024 alone, consistent with his classification as a Biden bundler since 2008.

Beyond FEC donations and SEC insider filings for Liz Claiborne (2007–2008), Karp's public financial footprint is effectively zero. Systematic searches across eight corporate registries, UCC filings, lobbying disclosures (LDA and FARA), OpenSanctions, Deutsche Bank DS10 transaction records, ICIJ offshore databases, ProPublica 990 nonprofit filings, and CourtListener returned no results. She has zero court appearances as a party under any name variation (Robbie Karp, Roberta Karp, Roberta Schuhalter Karp, Robin Karp). The only ACRIS property record linking her is the 2010 co-executor role for the Estate of Sondra Karp (doc 2010081200783001), in which she and Brad transferred 10 Park Avenue Apartment 14R to Brad at 115 Central Park West, using Paul Weiss's address at 1285 Avenue of the Americas for both executors. Brad subsequently sold the unit in 2018 for $505,000 (doc 2018071200423001). Post-Liz Claiborne, her SEC presence continues only through an advisory role at Aequi Acquisition Corp (CIK 0001823826), a growth-focused SPAC that raised its IPO in November 2020.
